elements.title: Outreach message
elements.what: A category-level invitation to an offline maker (Home & Kitchen manufacturers, Factory Launch Week, no ads, no listing fee) with a link to Meesho’s own sign-up. No product or demand numbers.
elements.why: Makers who aren’t on Meesho never hear of the launch; we can’t know their exact product from Udyam or IndiaMART data, so the invitation stays at the category.

elements.title: Demand teaser after onboarding
elements.what: On the onboarding finish screen, for the product type the maker just picked: orders a week going unserved and the buyers’ price band, or a neutral “no demand data yet”.
elements.why: The maker’s real question is “is there demand for what I make?”; we answer it once they’ve told us what they make.

elements.title: 5-minute cost check
elements.what: Inline on the finish screen: making cost → every fee (with the shipping choice from Pickup Address), break-even, take-home at any price, and whether a qualifying price exists.
elements.why: A maker decides on what they keep, not on the selling price, so we show take-home before they list anything.

elements.title: Seller-type question, moved to step 1
elements.what: Meesho’s own business-type question, asked right after the GST fetch instead of in the last step — unprompted on purpose: Meesho’s 7 options in Meesho’s order, nothing pre-selected, marked or hinted.
elements.why: The maker must declare it without a nudge; eligibility is decided only afterwards, by the GST nature of business and Udyam checks.

elements.title: GST and Udyam checks
elements.what: GST nature of business and Udyam activity are matched to the seller type → eligible, pending or not eligible. A verified manufacturer then lands on a finish screen: “What do you make?”
elements.why: Factory Launch is for real manufacturers, so records decide, not a self-declared answer. Resellers keep selling as today and go straight to the dashboard.

elements.title: Pack Point or self-ship
elements.what: Once the pickup address saves: a generic “Send one lot a week to a Pack Point” option with its status from the pincode (available / opening soon, no counts), and “See details & rate cards” opening a drawer: Pack Points near you sorted by distance, each with “₹30 per delivered order”, storage and services, and “Use this Pack Point” (picks the option on this step, with that location) or “Join waitlist” for one opening soon; then providers and rate cards. None nearby: “No Pack Point near you yet”. No product prices until the maker tells us what he makes.
elements.why: Many offline makers can’t pack and ship single orders; the Pack Point does it for the whole cluster.

elements.title: Create from photos
elements.what: A third way to upload, next to Single and Bulk: start a listing from a few phone photos.
elements.why: Listing is where new makers stall; photos are something every maker already has.

elements.title: Product screen, filled by the bot
elements.what: Category, cleaned-up images, title and attributes are pre-filled from the photos. The “We filled 21 details” card must be reviewed: yellow “Needs your review” until the maker opens the grouped list (pencil per detail, “Edited by you” tags), ticks “I’ve checked these details” and confirms; then green “Reviewed ✓ · 21 of 21”. Next stays disabled until then, any later edit sends it back to review, and the confirmation is stored with its date and time on the listing (shown in Catalog Uploads). “Fill demo values” never confirms.
elements.why: The bot does most of the typing, so the maker must own the result: a deliberate, recorded check of every pre-filled detail, with a record if a listing is disputed later.

elements.title: Demand and first lot
elements.what: Quantity screen: the maker’s minimum run and lead time, and a first lot suggested from his likely sales (≈ 2 weeks, never below his minimum run). The reasoning sits behind an (i) next to “First lot · 150 suggested”; no market totals, other makers’ commitments or confidence label on this screen.
elements.why: A maker needs one sensible number and the reason for it, not the market picture; the soft warning below his own minimum run stays.

elements.title: Take-home and Factory Launch status
elements.what: Price screen: making cost and margin in → every fee, break-even, list price and take-home, updated live. Under the result, a status banner: green “Qualifies for Factory Launch Week at this price”, yellow “Lists normally on Meesho · not eligible for Factory Launch at this price” (never by how much), or red “You’d lose ₹… per order” below break-even. Any price can go live. The bot’s own price shows its launch status at once; a price the maker types shows it only after “Check price”, three checks a day per product, so the cap can’t be found by trying prices. Fulfilment is switchable here for this product only: [Self-ship] [Pack Point] (Pack Point only in a live cluster), recalculating break-even, list price and take-home, with “+₹24 per order” and the rate-card drawer; the Packer detail follows the choice.
elements.why: Today the maker types a price with no fees or take-home shown, and Meesho accepts any price. Ours accepts any price too: it adds what they keep, a warning below break-even, and whether the price qualifies for Factory Launch, while the launch price cap stays hidden.

elements.title: Go-live checklist
elements.what: Images, details, bot details reviewed, price set and lot are ticked before Go live, with fees locked at dispatch. A separate line says “Factory Launch: Qualifies” or “Not eligible at this price”; it never blocks Go live. Listed above the cap, the listing sells as normal and Home and the order book say “Not eligible at this price · lower your price to join” → Price position.
elements.why: Today Submit Catalog sends the listing straight to QC; the checklist catches missing details first, and the payout matches the quote. Like today, the price never stops a listing: it only decides launch eligibility.

elements.title: EN / हिंदी toggle
elements.what: The listing bot’s screens switch between English and Hindi.
elements.why: The panel is English-only today; many makers are more at home in Hindi.

elements.title: Factory Launch tab
elements.what: A new event type in Promotions, next to Sale Events, Deals and Flash Events.
elements.why: Gives makers a launch route that asks for stock and a fair price, not a discount.

elements.title: Order book
elements.what: Slots per product type, expected orders per listing, suggested first lot, how much is committed so far, and the key dates.
elements.why: Makers commit stock against published demand. The price cap is checked at commit, never printed.

elements.title: Eligibility by rule
elements.what: Eligible makers just see Commit; a maker who fails a check sees “not eligible” and why.
elements.why: Entry is decided by records and price, not by who opts in.

elements.title: Commit stock
elements.what: Pick the SKU and the units (lot suggested, any number), the price is re-checked, then Commit. No discount field.
elements.why: A launch slot is earned with stock and a qualifying price.

elements.title: Factory Launch on Home, sidebar and Notices
elements.what: A banner at the top of Home (dates, slots left, an inline “Check my eligibility” checklist with one button per open step), a “Factory Launch” item under Boost Sales, and a pinned notice laid out like Meesho’s sale notices (the launch creative on top, then the offer, a status line that follows the maker’s state, and “Check my eligibility”) — only for makers who passed the checks.
elements.why: A new manufacturer finds the launch on day one instead of three clicks deep in Promotions, and always sees the one next step.

elements.title: Live launch view
elements.what: During the launch: orders each day against the expected range, and units sold of the committed lot.
elements.why: The maker sees the promised demand arrive, day by day.

elements.title: Listing-level quality score
elements.what: Quality shows a score for this listing, built from its own launch orders and returns.
elements.why: New listings show “No score available” today; launch orders build the listing’s own track record.

elements.title: Your listing’s own numbers
elements.what: The Business Dashboard’s existing tiles and product table, filled with the launched listing’s week.
elements.why: The growth loop reads numbers Meesho already shows each seller; nothing new is collected.

elements.title: Restock card
elements.what: On Inventory → Low Stock: run-rate, days of cover, reorder point, next batch, and dates to start and land it. “Plan this batch” opens a panel: units (any number, soft warning below the minimum run), start date → landing date from the lead time, cost at making price, ship from Self-ship / Pack Point, and days of cover after it lands; “Confirm plan” turns the card green (“Batch planned · 230 units · starts 21 Nov · lands 26 Nov”), and from the landing day the units join on-hand stock and the verdict is recomputed.
elements.why: Low Stock lists SKUs with no guidance today; the maker gets a dated production plan.

elements.title: SKU Health Coach
elements.what: One SKU, one cause, one fix a week, at the top of the Business Dashboard and on Home. “Change main photo” opens a panel: the current photo (with its click-through) beside the suggested one, cleaned to a white background, plus a shot tip; or upload another photo, cleaned the same way. “Apply” swaps the main image everywhere it shows (nothing else changes). The card turns green until the check a week later, then shows the next 7 days and the next fix (or none). Not applied after a week: the same fix, “Still pending”.
elements.why: The dashboard shows numbers only; the coach says what to change.

elements.title: Per-SKU funnel
elements.what: The coached SKU’s own views, clicks, orders and conversion — for the week the fix was given, and a week after it was applied (the result). The trigger that fired stays internal.
elements.why: The fix is tied to that listing’s numbers, not to seller-wide totals.

elements.title: Make-to-demand verdict
elements.what: A chip on each SKU in Inventory: Make more, Keep, Fix, Stop or Switch, with a one-line reason.
elements.why: Tells the maker what to produce next, not just what’s in stock.

elements.title: What to make instead
elements.what: For a SKU marked Stop: open-demand products on the same production line. “Plan a lot” on each suggestion opens a panel: open demand and confidence, likely orders for him (20% of the gap), a suggested first lot of ≈ 2 weeks of those orders, what buyers pay, units and a start date → ready date from his lead time; “Save plan” marks the card “Lot planned · 80 units · ready 26 Nov”, and “List it with photos” starts Create from photos with that product type already chosen.
elements.why: Factory time moves to products buyers are already asking for.

elements.title: Price position tab
elements.what: A Price position tab on Manage Pricing: Qualifies / Doesn’t qualify and which third of similar listings the price sits in (Low / Mid / High), never the cut-off. Two rules sit where they apply: the (i) next to “Price position” says the comparison is like-for-like (Factory Launch listings of the same material, size and type, per unit), and under the price field “You can change this price once a week” — after a change the field is locked with “Next change allowed on <date>”.
elements.why: Like-for-like keeps the comparison fair (a 1 L steel bottle against 1 L steel bottles, per unit). The weekly limit stops a maker probing for the hidden price cap by trying price after price and watching Qualifies flip.

elements.title: Price-hold breach
elements.what: If an edited price no longer qualifies: “slot removed” on Manage Pricing and the launch listing, with no number shown.
elements.why: The launch price has to hold after the launch, or buyers lose the saving.

elements.title: Cluster Pack Point program
elements.what: The Warehouse page gets two tabs for Factory-verified makers with a Pack Point within 150 km: “Meesho Warehouse” (unchanged) and “Cluster Pack Point” NEW (default if he ships through one). Inside: Overview, and once he’s on a Pack Point, Lots, Stock at Pack Point and Returns. “Switch to Pack Point” / “Use this Pack Point” opens a confirm panel in place (all or chosen products, each with its new take-home and launch status); after it, “You’re on Pack Point · <city> · first lot not sent yet” with “Plan first lot”, and the switched listings go back to “Needs your review”. “Switch back to self-ship” opens the reverse panel.
elements.why: Meesho Warehouse serves top sellers in three cities; makers in clusters need a shared node.

elements.title: Pack Points near you and the maker’s cost
elements.what: Pack Points near the maker, sorted by distance from his pickup pincode (“₹30 per delivered order” and “Use this Pack Point” at each open one, “Join waitlist” for one opening soon), beside his own cost at his Pack Point (making + fee + shipping and fixed fee + returns → break-even, take-home, list) and “Self-ship today” below it, each with its Factory Launch status (qualifies / not eligible at this price, never by how much). Storage: free for 30 days, then ₹0.29 per unit per day. No fee build-up, pool size or maker count.
elements.why: The maker needs what he pays, not how it’s built; the fee build-up and the 40-maker density gate are Meesho’s view (Behind it).

elements.title: Lots
elements.what: Cluster Pack Point → Lots: every lot as a row (Planned / In transit / Received), newest first, with “Plan a lot”. A row opens its detail: Samar’s D50 lot shows Expected 90 · Received 90 · Weighed 90 of 90 ✓ (the weight range in the (i)) · Stocked at Agra, the size split (UK 6–10) and “≈ 14 days of expected sales”.
elements.why: The lot is sized from demand, and weights at inbound make every later claim provable.

elements.title: Stock at Pack Point
elements.what: Cluster Pack Point → Stock at Pack Point: units on hand per product and size, days held, the free-storage end date (12 Jan 2027 for Samar’s D50 lot), then ₹0.29 per unit per day. On Inventory, a product stocked at a Pack Point carries an “At <city> Pack Point” tag.
elements.why: Today there is no view of stock held for the seller; the maker sees what sits at the node and when storage starts costing.

elements.title: Returns at the Pack Point
elements.what: Cluster Pack Point → Returns: returns received at the node, each weighed against its dispatch weight and graded A/B/C. Empty until he has returns.
elements.why: Return Tracking shows status only today; a weight and a grade decide who pays.

elements.title: Pack Point providers near the maker
elements.what: In the Pack Point drawer: the fulfilment providers serving the maker’s pincode (WareIQ, Prozo, Eshopbox, Shiprocket Fulfillment), each with services (bulk in · pack · returns) and a rate card (Shiprocket ₹24 per order; others on request), under the Pack Points near him.
elements.why: A maker compares the shared Pack Point with the providers already serving his area before choosing; rates are shown as published, with nothing invented.
